facts.F1: ADO Story 6135: Upgrade Lighthouse from .NET 10 to .NET 11 in one change, now that .NET 11.0.0 is GA (2026-11-10, SDK 11.0.100) and Npgsql.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL 11.0.0 is released. Retarget all four projects, SDK pins, Docker images and the .NET-versioned packages together, and remove the Renovate .NET 10 hold.
facts.F10: Build pipelines verify the app on .NET 11
facts.F11: the SDK pins and toolchain pin checks name .NET 11
facts.F12: the SQLite and Postgres verify builds, E2E and Sonar run
facts.F13: all are green with no new Sonar issue; a pipeline that still installs SDK 10 falsifies this
facts.F14: Docker image and standalone builds serve the app
facts.F15: the Dockerfile uses the 11.0 images and the standalone workflows use the 11 SDK
facts.F16: the image is built and started, and a standalone package is built and started
facts.F17: each serves the app and reports a .NET 11 runtime; a build or start failure falsifies this
facts.F19: the .NET 10 hold rule is removed from renovate.json
facts.F2: Lighthouse runs on .NET 11 with unchanged behaviour, so self-hosters get the current runtime and Renovate can keep the .NET stack current again.
facts.F21: no rule holds back .NET packages or images, and the remaining docs and pins that name .NET 10 as current now name .NET 11; historical briefs and decision records stay unchanged
facts.F22: Retarget the four projects to net11.0; move the .NET-versioned packages to 11.x; change SDK pins in the build action and the standalone packaging and SBOM workflows; update the Dockerfile images, Start-DevServer.ps1 path, the Sonar gates workflow, toolchain pin test, solution file, perf readings files, examine script, regenerated SBOM, ARCHITECTURE.md, CLAUDE.md and the two user docs; remove the Renovate .NET 10 hold; check migrations via Create-Migration.ps1, Stryker.NET config and standalone packaging.
facts.F23: Adopting new .NET 11 APIs, for example the first-class cookie Partitioned property that Program.cs works around today. Possible follow-up only.
facts.F24: Any change to routes, DTO shapes, serialized responses, UI pixels or topologies; this is a behaviour-free upgrade.
facts.F25: Historical architecture briefs, diagrams and decision records that name .NET 10 as history stay unchanged. Release notes are written at release time, not here.
facts.F26: DISCOVER and DIVERGE are skipped for this Feature.
facts.F27: The work item gets the Release Notes tag with one short line at release time: Lighthouse now runs on .NET 11.
facts.F28: The Quint scenario exploration is not relevant for any of the three values: each has a settled happy path with no refusal, race or stale-input case.
facts.F29: The retarget and the package majors form one slice, because splitting them leaves the build broken. The other slices only check or clean up what follows.
facts.F3: A self-hoster runs Lighthouse on .NET 11 and sees no change in behaviour: the same routes, responses, screens and data. Settings, System Info shows the .NET 11 runtime version.
facts.F30: No UI sketch is needed: no screen changes. Settings, System Info reads the runtime version at run time and shows .NET 11 with no code change; test fixtures that say .NET 10.0.0 there are values, not pins.
facts.F31: Platform and hosting only: no bounded context model, glossary term, domain event or UI surface is touched; RBAC, Lighthouse-Clients and the website need no change. The usage-data event question belongs to DEVOPS.
facts.F32: The maintainer retargets the projects and packages, then runs the backend suite and dev server
facts.F34: The maintainer pushes and the verify builds, E2E and Sonar run on SDK 11
facts.F35: The self-hoster pulls the new Docker image or standalone package and the app runs as before
facts.F37: A maintainer runs the full backend suite and the dev server on net11.0: every test passes, no migration reports a pending model change, and Settings, System Info shows a .NET 11 runtime.
facts.F38: Backend, tests and migrations run on .NET 11 with unchanged behaviour
facts.F39: A maintainer pushes the change: the SQLite and Postgres verify builds, E2E and Sonar run on the .NET 11 SDK and are green with no new Sonar issue.
facts.F4: The maintainer can build, test and package Lighthouse with the .NET 11 SDK in every pipeline, and Renovate proposes .NET 11 updates again.
facts.F40: Every pipeline builds and verifies on .NET 11
facts.F41: A self-hoster builds and starts the Docker image, and a standalone package for Linux, macOS or Windows: each serves the app on a .NET 11 runtime.
facts.F42: Self-hosted image and standalone builds run on .NET 11
facts.F43: A maintainer reads renovate.json and the docs: no rule holds back .NET, and current-state docs and pins name .NET 11 while history stays unchanged.
facts.F44: Renovate keeps the .NET stack current and the docs match the runtime
facts.F5: The self-hosted Docker image and the Linux, macOS and Windows standalone builds run on .NET 11 and serve the app.
facts.F6: Backend runs on .NET 11 with the full suite green
facts.F7: all four projects target net11.0 with .NET 11 package versions
facts.F8: the full backend suite runs, Integration included, and the app starts from the dev server script
